ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is a voltage source labeled δ(t), with the positive terminal on top; the upper branch has a 1 H inductor and a 1 Ω resistor connected in series from left to right; the right-side node is connected to the lower reference line through a 1 F capacitor, and the output is labeled Vc(t), namely the capacitor voltage. Then reason: the problem gives zero initial conditions, and the Laplace transform of the unit impulse input is Vs(s)=1. The impedances of the components are ZL=sL=s, ZR=1, ZC=1/(sC)=1/s. By the voltage division relationship of the series circuit, Vc(s)=Vs(s)·ZC/(ZL+ZR+ZC)=(1/s)/(s+1+1/s)=1/(s^2+s+1). Complete the square in the denominator: s^2+s+1=(s+1/2)^2+3/4=(s+1/2)^2+(√3/2)^2. method.method_draft: From the image set L=1, R=1, C=1 and note the capacitor voltage is the output. From the text use zero initial conditions and source voltage vs(t)=δ(t). Write KVL: δ(t)=L di/dt+Ri+vc, with i=C dvc/dt, giving vc''+vc'+vc=δ(t). For t>0 the forcing is zero, so solve vc''+vc'+vc=0. Determine post-impulse data by integrating the ODE across t=0: the capacitor voltage remains vc(0+)=0, while vc'(0+)-vc'(0-)=1; with zero initial conditions vc'(0+)=1. The characteristic roots are -1/2±j√3/2, so vc(t)=e^{-t/2}(A cos(√3t/2)+B sin(√3t/2)); applying vc(0+)=0 and vc'(0+)=1 gives A=0, B=2/√3, hence Vc(t)=(2/√3)e^{-t/2}sin((√3/2)t).
